newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER SHOWCASE-TACTICS OF BARCELONA V ATLETICO MATCH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-TACTICS OF BARCELONA V ATLETICO MATCH.

text.p: A look at the strengths and weaknesses of Barcelona and Atletico Madrid who meet on Saturday in the Camp Nou stadium (1930 GMT).
Barcelona

Strategy: Bobby Robson has begun the season with a 4-5-1 formation, in which Josep Guardiola and Gheorghe Popescu play in front of the back four to provide the link with midfield. Giovanni plays a central coordinating role up-front, with Ronaldo normally as the solitary target man.
But Juan Pizzi will step straight into the centre-forward position now Ronaldo has failed to recover in time from a leg injury.
Strengths: Barcelona's main strength has been Ronaldo who has already scored 12 league goals, most of them after beating players with runs from well outside the area.
In his absence, Giovanni is a probably their potential match-winner. The injuries mean Robson will have to call on his talented substitutes' bench, which contains several internationals.

Weaknesses: Over-reliance on Ronaldo. His absence may undermine them badly. Equally, the absence of goalkeeper Vitor Baia is a major blow as Carlos Busquets is widely viewed as unreliable. Winger Luis Figo, also away playing for Portugal, is another significant absentee.

The crowd at the Camp Nou can sometimes be highly vocal in its frustration, even if their side is winning, and the pressure can prove too much at times, especially for temperamental players like Ivan de la Pena.

Motivation: Barcelona are still smarting from their Cup final loss and two comprehensive league defeats to Atletico last season and will be out to prove themselves in the first big test of their domestic campaign. Over 100,000 fans will be there feeling the same way.
Atletico Madrid

Strategy: Atletico play a fairly orthodox 4-4-2 formation, with Kiko Narvaez generally playing behind fellow striker Juan Eduardo Esnaider and Juan Vizcaino linking defence and midfield. The back four tends to push well forward to decrease opponents' room for manoeuvre, while goalkeeper Jose Molina does a sweeper's job, cleaning up at the back.

Traditionally Atletico have been a counter-attacking unit, happy to sit back and wait for their opponents to attack while Barcelona and Real Madrid have been ball-playing sides that try to control the game.
Radomir Antic's Atletico are no exception to this rule and rely heavily on speedy bursts out of defence, while patient build-up work is comparatively rare.

Strengths: Charismatic coach Radomir Antic turned round relegation candidates into a double-winning side and, as an unrivalled motivator, continues to be the single most important factor behind Atletico's success.
The player that best characterises this adrenalin-charged approach is Argentina captain Diego Simeone, one of the most relentless tacklers and support players in world football.

Molina is a powerful force at the back and led a solid if unspectacular defensive unit that was Spain's meanest last season. In midfield, Caminero's vision and Kiko's cheeky improvisation are both potential match-winners, while Pantic's devilish right foot has made set-pieces a major source of goals.

Weaknesses: Although the back four, as well as Simeone and Vizcaino, are dependable characters, too many of Atletico's players are temperamental. Lopez, Caminero and Esnaider in particular are all known to lose their heads and get sent off, and -- along with Pantic -- have far too many off days.

Atletico lack the strength in depth of Barcelona and Real, who usually leave a couple of internationals on the bench and several more in the stands. As a consequence, Atletico have no set-piece man to fill in for Pantic if the Serb is unable to recover from injury for Saturday's game.
Atletico escaped last season without major injury problems but will always be vulnerable in this department because of their inferior spending power.
Molina's tendency to play well outside his goal leaves him vulnerable to long distance lobs, a speciality of Barcelona's de la Pena.

Motivation: Defeat would leave Atletico 13 points behind Barcelona after just 12 games. No champion wants to be told they are facing their heirs apparent, which is the way most Spaniards see Bobby Robson's Barcelona.
